messages:
maria: Heads-up — planned maintenance for eu-west-2 GPU pools: staggered node cordons + NIC microcode update + rolling reboots. Window: Wed 03:00-06:00 UTC. Expect ~10% capacity impact per AZ while racks drain, and short tail latency spikes on long-running streams. We'll do per-rack canaries, then parallelize across remaining racks.
kevin: copying. do we have a hard SLO we need to meet for hosted traffic? can we fallback traffic automatically to us-west?
maria: hosted API critical tenants will be routed to us-west by smart-routing policy. non-critical customers may see higher latency. SLOs: we'll keep error rate <0.5% but latency P99 may spike ~200-400ms for a few minutes during uncordon/warmup.
samir: i'll run the canary on rack-r03 and rack-r04 first. plan to verify kv-cache warmup and token throughput before continuing.
li: cost note — if we need to spin additional dedicated backfill, reserved capacity billing doesn't change but spot backfill could add ephemeral spend. estimate: ~$150-300 extra for 3hr window if we double backfill.
jess: customer-success will send a targeted notice to enterprise tenants with Dedicated and Private deployments. can you drop the customer-facing blurb here after finalizing the start time?
maria: will post blurb. also adding runbook + commands below. please review.

maria: Runbook excerpt:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-<id> -n gpu-pool
kubectl drain gpu-node-<id> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n gpu-pool
# apply firmware (vendor tool)
/vendor/fwtool apply --node gpu-node-<id> --fw v2.3.1
# reboot
ssh gpu-node-<id> sudo reboot
# verify: warmup job
kubectl label nodes gpu-node-<id> warmed=true
bash ops/warmup/gpu_warmup.sh --node gpu-node-<id>
```

kevin: nit: add a `kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/<node>` step after warmup to avoid routing flaps.
maria: good call, i'll add it.

oncall-bot: maintenance: created maintenance-1768501234 (eu-west-2 gpu pools). Assigned: ops-rotation. Incident stub: #M-1768501234
ops-rotation: ack — i'll be primary oncall for the window. will follow runbook and post progress updates here.
samir: quick question — what's the rollback? if fwtool fails, are we skipping reboot and leaving nodes drained until vendor patch? or reimage to previous snapshot?
maria: rollback: if fwtool step fails we will revert to previous microcode where possible or reimage from last golden snapshot. worst-case: keep node drained and shift capacity. decision tree is in the runbook link (ops/runbooks/fw-microcode.md)
kevin: any network config changes tied to the NIC update? we need to watch for MTU or qos changes.
li: vendor notes say no config changes expected, just microcode. still, we should monitor packet drops and retransmits on eth0 for 30m post-reboot.
jess: sending draft customer blurb:
"Planned maintenance in eu-west-2 for GPU hosts on Wed 03:00-06:00 UTC. We expect brief performance impacts for some workloads. Hosted API will route critical traffic to fallback region. No action required. Contact support if you have SLA concerns." 
maria: perfect — small edit and we can send.

kevin: operational tweak proposal: temporarily lower batch window for inference router to reduce P99 spike during warmup. ops/warmup team ok with that?
samir: ok from my side. i'll coordinate with routing team at T-20.

maria: final checklist: 
- [x] vendor firmware package validated on test rack
- [x] runbook link added
- [x] canary engineers: samir + kevin
- [x] oncall assigned: ops-rotation
- [ ] customer notice: jess to send at T-24

ops-rotation: will post progress: starting canary 03:00 UTC -> status updates every 10m. escalate to oncall manager if >10% unexpected pod evictions.
kevin: noted. i'll prepare autoscale policy toggle: set min spare nodes +2 for window.
li: i'll monitor net metrics and post alerts to this thread if packet errors >0.5% baseline.

maria: thanks all. i'll pin the runbook and the maintenance stub. ping here if anything changes. :thumbsup:
summary: maintenance plan for eu-west-2 GPU pool: staggered cordon, NIC microcode update, rolling reboots, canaries and routing fallback
